takeaway: Bicarbonate carries 80 to 90 per cent of the blood's carbon dioxide; carbonic anhydrase in red cells makes it.

question.text: Carbon dioxide is principally transported in the blood in which form?
question.say: Carbon dioxide is principally transported in the blood in which form?

lines.text: Carbon dioxide needs a ride through the blood.
lines.say: Little carbon dioxide wants a ride through the river of blood.
The big ferry is full of passengers. This is bicarbonate.

lines.text: It carries 80 to 90 per cent of the CO2.
lines.say: Bicarbonate accounts for about eighty to ninety per cent of the carbon dioxide in the blood.

lines.text: Carbamino compounds carry 5 to 10 per cent; 5 per cent is dissolved.
lines.say: Carbamino compounds carry five to ten per cent, and only five per cent is physically dissolved.

lines.text: Red cells use carbonic anhydrase, with zinc, to make it.
lines.say: Red cells hold carbonic anhydrase, which needs zinc as a cofactor, to turn carbon dioxide into bicarbonate.

lines.text: Remember: carbon dioxide travels mostly as bicarbonate.
lines.say: Remember: carbon dioxide travels mostly as bicarbonate.
